title: What Makes a Good Medical Image Tokenizer? Rethinking Reconstruction and Generation in Medical Image Tokenization
abstract: arXiv:2609.24691v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Latent diffusion models now dominate medical image generation, and every such pipeline rests on a \emph{tokenizer} that compresses images into the latent codes for image generation to operate on. Thereby, the tokenizer choice bounds every downstream task from reconstruction fidelity and generation quality to the representations available for downstream analysis. Yet, medical imaging pipelines routinely utilize tokenizers from natural imaging on the hypothesis that their behavior carries over. However, this is an assumption never tested in the medical imaging regime, where datasets are orders of magnitude smaller and images exhibit far lower inter-sample variance. We present a systematic evaluation of medical image tokenizers evaluating thirty configurations across ten model families on twelve datasets at three compression factors, spanning reconstruction, generation, latent geometry, downstream classification, and memorization. translated_title: 什么造就了好的医学图像分词器？重新思考医学图像分词中的重建与生成
translated_abstract: 潜在扩散模型如今主导着医学图像生成，而每一个这样的流程都依赖于一个分词器，它将图像压缩成潜在编码以供图像生成使用。因此，分词器的选择限制了每一个下游任务——从重建保真度、生成质量到可用于下游分析的表示。然而，医学成像流程通常直接沿用来自自然图像领域的分词器，并假设其行为可以迁移。然而，这一假设从未在医学成像领域得到验证，因为医学成像中数据集要小几个数量级，且图像样本间的方差要低得多。我们对医学图像分词器进行了系统性评估，在三个压缩因子下，对十个模型家族的三十种配置在十二个数据集上进行了评估，涵盖重建、生成、潜在空间几何、下游分类和记忆化等方面。我们发现
tldr: 本文对医学图像分词器进行了系统性评估，指出自然图像分词器直接迁移到医学成像领域的假设从未被验证，并在多种模型、数据集和压缩因子下全面考察了分词器对重建、生成、潜在空间几何、下游分类和记忆化的影响。
en_tdlr: This paper presents a systematic evaluation of medical image tokenizers across model families, datasets, and compression factors, challenging the untested assumption that natural image tokenizers transfer well to medical imaging with its smaller datasets and lower inter-sample variance.
